title: Scheduling Electricity Production Units to Mitigate Severe Weather Impact: An Efficient Computational Implementation
summary: Extreme weather events in electric power systems can cause line trips or physical damage to transmission infrastructure, potentially leading to large-scale load shedding. To mitigate this risk, we propose a framework that strategically pre-positions the commitment of generation units--particularly slow-start units--to adapt to transmission topologies that may arise following such events. The objective is to minimize load shedding under worst-case conditions. This paper makes two main contributions.
